entry.title: two down
entry.content:
I am two books down! Well… not as such. Three and a bit. But this is my first retrospective of a potential several, and I wanted to use each little connected series of books in the Discworld setting as milestones. Might end up breaking the longer ones into smaller milestones, but it is what it is.

Reading has been incredibly therapeutic, and for Going Postal it was very nostalgic. I haven’t had this kind of motivation to read in years! In fact, I did the math, and I’ve read more since the beginning of 2026 than I have for the entire sum of many previous years combined. Not just in terms of raw number of books, you can see that plain as day on the bookshelf page. Not exactly the most advanced math to figure that out. But also in terms of pages, real volume of literature.

You could read a dozen short stories and record each and every title and still read less than one truly chunky novel. The Discworld books are varying in size, but they generally hover around three or four hundred pages, and I’ve still been going through them extremely quickly.

That being said, I think I’m going to try to take it a little bit slower. Reading quickly is fun! Reading quickly is good! Reading quickly is liable to get me through all of Discworld before summer. I would prefer to savor these books a little bit more. So for the sake of having books to read come June, I am going to try to finish books a little slower than one every few days.

I am fully aware that there probably isn’t anyone reading these blogs, by the by. I don’t mind that. This is more of a publicly-visible journal than anything else for me.
entry.summary: I am making my way through my books shockingly fast

entry.title: books!
entry.content:
Humble Bundle, as of me writing this, has a bundle with 39 of Terry Pratchett’s Discworld books for extremely cheap. Discworld has been one of my favorite settings in literature, though I have only read a handful of the books.

Well… now I have a chance to reread those books and more! I intend on reading all 39 of the books I have just gotten my hands on. It’s not the entirety of the Discworld collection, but it’s more than enough, and it includes the vast majority of the best books from it.

I’m starting with Going Postal, one of my favorites and one of the earliest Discworld memories I have. But keep an eye on my bookshelf collection for those books as I finish and continue chewing through the bundle.
entry.summary: I have quite a lot of books to read now. I'm excited

entry.title: looking forward
entry.content:
As I write this post I am waiting outside a classroom at the university that I attend, as prepared as I can reasonably expect to be for the very last final exam that I have before I graduate. It’s something that I had stressed over the last few days. It’s the last obstacle before I recieve my Bachelor’s Degree, after all. But I’m prepared. I’ve done well in this class so far, and I’m going to succeed.

Even so, though, I think I would do well looking forward, past today, to think about what comes next. Because, after all, I have to keep moving forward.

I have a few job applications pending, but they’ve been waiting for quite a while. If I’m being honest, the job market is atrocious in my area at the moment. Every software development related job is one of three things: a senior position I don’t qualify for because I don’t have enough experience, a position that requires a security clearance that I do not have, or a job that I have already applied for. Even so, there’s a few remote jobs I’m waiting on, as well as some jobs that are a little bit less related to my field of study that I’ve more recenty applied to.

I’m not all that optimistic, that’s just the way I am, but I am hopeful. Because no matter what happens tomorrow, if I keep trying, I’ll make it eventually. So I have to keep trying.
entry.summary: Thinking about the future as I prepare to graduate.
